newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl party wants top German tax rate of 35 pct.
newsitem.headline: Kohl party wants top German tax rate of 35 pct.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) want to cut the top German income tax rate to 35 percent from 53 percent under a reform planned for 1999, the Bild am Sonntag newspaper said on Sunday.

The entry rate for taxpayers would also be reduced to below 20 percent from 25.9 percent under a proposal drafted by Kohl's parliamentary lieutenant Wolfgang Schaeuble to be discussed at a CDU party conference in late October.
The newspaper added that the cuts would reduce the income tax burden by 20 to 30 billion marks, but would be offset by the scrapping of 50 billion marks worth of tax breaks.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel, said by Bild to have agreed on the proposal's key terms, said in Washington on Saturday he would call in a speech on Monday for a cut in the top rate to below 40 percent.
Waigel, of the Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU) recently rejected calls by the government coalition's Free Democrat (FDP) junior partners for a major tax reform in 1998.

But a broad consensus emerged over the summer on the need for Germany to impose sweeping reforms to a system seen as imposing a heavy burden on ordinary taxpayers while offering loopholes to the wealthy.
